extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, current NIH award recipients, institutional grants administrators, and NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH Grants Policy Statement and related NIH policy topics that define terms and conditions of NIH grant awards and the compliance requirements applicants and recipients must follow. Covers clinical trials, human subjects, data sharing, conflicts of interest, animal welfare, fiscal policy, peer review, and other award conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Grants Policy Statement (NIHGPS) — Scope Note
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIHGPS makes available, in a single document, the policy requirements that serve as the terms and conditions of NIH grant awards. By accepting an award, recipients agree to comply with the requirements in the NIHGPS except where the notice of award states otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices of policy changes published in the NIH Guide for Grants and Contracts can supersede information in the NIHGPS; compliance with those policy updates also becomes a term and condition of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Policy Changes supplanting NIHGPS
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of policy changes published in the NIH Guide for Grants and Contracts may supersede the NIHGPS and become binding terms and conditions of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must monitor and comply with NIH Guide notices; the NIHGPS is updated annually to incorporate such notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Conditions and Information for NIH Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Web page information that serves as additional terms and conditions of award that apply in addition to the NIHGPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees must follow award-specific conditions described on the Award Conditions and Information page in addition to NIHGPS requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Requirements for Grants and Contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements governing NIH-funded clinical trials, including NIH's definition of a clinical trial, decision tools to determine trial status, registration and reporting obligations, and clinical-trial specific funding and review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: NIH's Definition of a Clinical Trial; Decision Tool: Does Your Human Subjects Study Meet the NIH Definition of a Clinical Trial?; Clinical Trial-Specific Funding Opportunities; Clinical Trial-Specific Review Criteria; Good Clinical Practice training; Human Subjects System; posting informed consent forms; protocol templates; and steps to compliance for registering and reporting on ClinicalTrials.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH's Definition of a Clinical Trial and Decision Tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides the official NIH definition of a clinical trial and tools to help determine whether a project meets that definition (including BESH vs. observational distinctions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators must use NIH decision tools (e.g., 'Is My Project a Clinical Trial, Basic Experimental Study Involving Humans (BESH), or an Observational Study?') to classify studies for application and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Registering & Reporting NIH-Funded Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandates for registering clinical trials and for reporting results and other required information to ClinicalTrials.gov or other designated registries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes policy and regulation on ClinicalTrials.gov registration and reporting, NIH policy on dissemination of NIH-funded clinical trial information, and steps to compliance for awardees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Research — Definitions and Processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and decision tools for human subjects research and guidance on pre-award and post-award processes for projects involving human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: Decision Tool: Am I Doing Human Subjects Research?; Human Subjects Research infographics; Just In Time (JIT) information; study monitoring and progress reporting; and related training and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of Confidentiality (CoC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about protections afforded by Certificates of Confidentiality for NIH-funded research and investigator/institutional responsibilities regarding CoCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes what information is protected, investigator responsibilities, and applicability for NIH-funded and non-NIH-funded research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Policies for Human Subjects Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies requiring appropriate inclusion of specified participant populations in NIH-funded human subjects research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes policies and guidance on Inclusion of Women and Minorities, Valid Analysis for NIH-defined Phase III Clinical Trials, Inclusion Across the Lifespan, and other inclusion-related requirements and related reviewer/applicant guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single IRB (sIRB) Requirement for Multi-site Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on use of a single institutional review board for multi-site or cooperative research to streamline IRB review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes case studies and implementation guidance for sIRB policy compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Training Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for training in Good Clinical Practice for personnel engaged in NIH-funded clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the clinical trial requirements; applicants/awardees should document GCP training as required by funding opportunity or NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and guidance designed to strengthen rigor and reproducibility in preclinical research and grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Principles and Guidelines for Publishing Preclinical Research, Guidance for Rigor and Reproducibility in Grant Applications, resources for preparing applications, and training/workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Data Management and Sharing Policy (DMSP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy requiring a Data Management & Sharing Plan for NIH-funded research that generates scientific data, and expectations for making data accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes writing a data management & sharing plan, budgeting for data management & sharing, selecting repositories, sharing approaches, and considerations for privacy and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genomic Data Sharing Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations and requirements for sharing genomic data from NIH-funded research, including how to develop genomic data sharing plans and where to submit genomic data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Genomic Data Sharing Policy overview, institution-specific expectations, data submission and release expectations, registration and submission to dbGaP, and the NIH Genomic Data User Code of Conduct and Data Use Certification Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and Protection of Participant Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and best practices for protecting participant privacy, including considerations for designating data for controlled access and informed consent considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers considerations for obtaining informed consent, controlled-access designation, and special considerations for working with AI/AN communities and other sensitive populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing and Using NIH Controlled-Access Data Repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and procedures for accessing controlled-access scientific and genomic data from NIH repositories and obligations of users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirements for NIH data use agreements, dbGaP access procedures, and responsibilities of data users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy requiring that NIH-funded research publications be submitted to PubMed Central and made publicly available according to NIH public access requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes overview of the policy and instructions for submitting manuscripts to PubMed Central and contacts for policy help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory requirements and training expectations for financial conflicts of interest for recipients of NIH funds, including special highlights for foreign institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes FCOI training requirements, important regulatory highlights, and links to NIH Guide notices related to FCOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Disclosure of Other Support, Foreign Components, and Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for disclosing other support, foreign components of research, and potential conflicts that could affect NIH-funded projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related to foreign interference policies and processes for handling allegations; applicants and awardees must fully disclose other support and foreign collaborations per NIH requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Interference — Disclosure and Handling Process
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policies and processes addressing foreign interference, including requirements for disclosure of other support and foreign components and processes for handling allegations related to foreign interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides notices, statements, reports, and institutional processes for reporting and handling concerns about foreign interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Integrity and Misconduct Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH expectations, definitions, and procedures for research integrity, responsible conduct of research (RCR), and handling allegations of research misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Integrity and Confidentiality in Peer Review, Taking Action – Case Studies in Research Integrity, reporting processes for concerns, and NIH actions/oversight after findings of misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Property Policy and Bayh-Dole Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing intellectual property arising from NIH-funded research and recipient obligations under Bayh-Dole regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers invention reporting, patent rights, obligations to promote practical application of inventions, and institutional certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Organism Sharing Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for sharing model organisms developed with NIH funding to facilitate reproducibility and further research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy explains obligations for making model organisms available and how sharing plans should be addressed in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Tools Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on sharing research tools (e.g., software, reagents) developed with NIH funding to enable broader use and validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on appropriate sharing mechanisms and expectations for accessibility of research tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawards and Subrecipient Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and expectations governing subawards, including responsibilities of prime awardees and requirements for subrecipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes submission policies and administrative requirements for managing subawards under NIH grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on application and post-award submission requirements and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers required forms, timing, Just In Time information, and other submission-related instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and requirements related to the possession, use, and transfer of select agents and toxins in NIH-funded research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees must comply with applicable select agent regulations and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting a Safe and Respectful Workplace
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations, policies, and requirements to maintain a safe and respectful workplace on NIH-funded projects, including processes for handling allegations of harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes institutional reporting, what to expect when notifying NIH, definitions, data collection for sexual harassment and sex discrimination, and related NIH oversight actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Policies and Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing NIH peer review, including management of conflicts of interest, simplified review frameworks, reviewer guidance, and applicant guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes background information on the NIH peer review process, simplified review frameworks for most Research Project Grants (RPGs), and separate guidance for reviewers and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Stage Investigator (ESI) Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies that define Early Stage Investigator status, eligibility extensions, and implications for funding and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes how to determine ESI status, extension policies, and lists of grant mechanisms that preserve ESI status.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Fiscal Policies (salary cap, NRSA stipends, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiscal policies applicable to NIH awards, including salary cap summaries, NRSA stipends, and other fiscal notices and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides historical salary cap summaries and notices that affect budgeting and award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools and Resources (eRA, Glossary, FAQs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational resources and help (e.g., eRA systems, glossary, FAQs) to support compliance with NIH policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIH-provided tools and help pages for technical issues, policy clarifications, and submission support.
